post_topic: Why LLM-agnostic design with HITL governance isn't optional for production AI systems — it's the only architecture that survives contact with the enterprise
scene_description: A split architectural diagram contrasts two system designs side by side: on the left, a fragile demo-oriented stack where an LLM (labeled GPT-4o / Claude 3.5 / Gemini Ultra) connects directly to business logic with a cache storing pending HITL states, showing a TTL expiration erasing a human review action; on the right, the Cloud Decoded production architecture showing an abstraction interface layer in front of the LLM, a durable execution layer holding the HITL state machine with pending/approved/rejected states and logged rejection reasons feeding back into prompt context, and tenant-scoped infrastructure boundaries preventing context bleed. The tension is between a system architected for the demo and one architected for a compliance officer.
